title: The market’s words, not the reader’s
blurb: Somebody types “a free competitive landscape research tool” and we searched for exactly that, which finds articles about the idea rather than the market. The market says “competitive intelligence software”. Reading the titles of searches an analysis already sends, every two-to-four word phrase is counted once per independent site — forty pages from one content farm is not agreement — and the answer is the longest phrase that extends the one the most sites agreed on. Deterministic, no model, and shown to a reader as an interpretation rather than assumed.
